races.name: Molson Coors Mares' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Crokes Cross
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up profile for Stuart Coltherd; won on soft/good at 2m previously but Cartmel's short run-in is a recurring issue for deep closers, and 87 days off the track combined with a modest recent form string (701-) gives cause for caution on fitness.

runners_data.name: Eremenko
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson's 5yo has solid form in similar trips and going (2W2P in comparable conditions), travels prominently which is the ideal style for today's likely pace shape, and Theo Gillard takes the ride fresh off a productive 71-day break — the stable's T14 rate of 7/33 is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Cinating
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 4yo won last time out on soft and Sean Bowen is a significant booking; she does carry a fall in her recent history and the Good ground is slightly different from her wins on softer surfaces, but her OR of 120 and recent winning form make her one of the most dangerous challengers in the race.

runners_data.name: Letmeseethecolts
runners_data.note: Came into the race having fallen at the final flight last time (19F), which is a significant jumping concern over hurdles; best form came on Good ground at shorter trips and Nathan Moscrop takes over, but there is a strong case that the extra yardage at 2m1f is at the limit of her comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Millena Agent
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed pace-setter, Mark Walford's 6yo carries a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting the prominent role is slightly outside her optimal profile; ran just 7 days ago and the quick turnaround alongside a T14 figure of 0/17 for the stable is a concern, though unchallenged in front she could last longer than her odds suggest.

runners_data.name: Order Another One
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 5yo with an UNKNOWN going profile and a pulled-up run on her most recent start (42 days ago); her win last time before that (S344-1 form) is intriguing but Peter Kavanagh rides for a stable with no recent runners so there is little data to anchor confidence.

runners_data.name: Rachel Lopez
runners_data.note: Stuart Coltherd's second runner is a hold-up type who ran just 7 days ago; her form on similar Good ground reads 3/4 placed runs but no wins in that context, and the tight Cartmel track with its short run-in limits the value of a deep hold-up approach from OR 120.

runners_data.name: Raincloud
runners_data.note: Michael Chapman's 6yo wears a tongue-strap and has a true hold-up profile that has been shifted to midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate every closer at the rear — his natural finishing position may be denied in this shape, compounding a career form line that reads 8,8,11,9,8 on similar going.

runners_data.name: Big Gypsy King
runners_data.note: James Moffatt's 4yo has a flagged tendency to fade in the finish and his natural hold-up style has also been mapped to midfield for the same overcrowding reason as Raincloud; his historical going form of 4-9th in comparable conditions and an amateur jockey booking (Leah Noreci, 10lb claim) make this a difficult ride in an already awkward tactical position.

runners_data.name: Echinacea
runners_data.note: Noel C Kelly's 4yo travels prominently, which suits today's race shape, and has placed twice on similar surfaces; the OR 120 rating combined with Derek Fox in the saddle (experienced jumps jockey) gives this mare a real chance if she improves on her last two runs (9th and 4th on Good ground at similar trips).

races.paceDynamic: Millena Agent is the sole confirmed front-runner and, despite a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting she is somewhat out of her natural role at this trip, she is likely to stride into a clear lead and set a sustainable, controlled tempo on Good ground at Cartmel. With no other genuine pace-setter to press her, the early fractions will be honest rather than gruelling, meaning the leader will not be unnecessarily softened up before the final climb. The field also contains Raincloud and Big Gypsy King, both natural hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield because the race cannot accommodate all the closers at the rear — their true finishing kicks may therefore be compromised if they cannot settle as far back as they prefer. This shape — a lone front-runner, uncontested, on a fair pace — strongly favours prominent racers and those who travel smoothly just off the lead, giving them a position from which to challenge without having to produce a wide-sweeping finish.

scenarios.title: Millena Agent Controls

scenarios.body: If Millena Agent secures the lead unchallenged and the field settles into a steady single-file procession.

scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Millena Agent fades in the final half-mile and a horse travelling in second or third sweeps past her on the hill.
scenarios.body: If Millena Agent fades in the final half-mile and a horse travelling in second or third sweeps past her on the hill.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected and the front rank weakens significantly over the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected and the front rank weakens significantly over the final two hurdles.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners fall, unseat or the pace scenario collapses through early interference.
scenarios.body: If multiple runners fall, unseat or the pace scenario collapses through early interference.

watchPoints.text: Millena Agent's jumping must be monitored from the first — if she makes an early error and loses the lead, the entire pace shape collapses and the race becomes far more unpredictable for every runner behind her.

Cinating carries a recent fall in her form string; if she jumps poorly or repeats that tendency, Sean Bowen may be unable to maintain her prominent position, costing her the ideal striking point on the final bend.

Letmeseethecolts fell at the last flight on her most recent run — watch her jumping throughout, particularly at the final hurdle where the race is likely to be decided, as a repeat could cause interference to the horses tracking her.

Raincloud and Big Gypsy King are both natural hold-up horses mapped to midfield — if either drifts back to their true position early, they may find themselves too far off the pace on a track where Cartmel's short home straight gives insufficient room to close.

Order Another One is a wild card: lightly raced, stable with no recorded recent runners and a going profile marked UNKNOWN — watch the market moves at the off, as any support could indicate connections hold a significant private form line not visible in the public record.

races.name: Burlington Stone Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Fine As Wine
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has placed twice in six sim-going runs but has not won on Good; trainer Gary Hanmer is 0/6 in the past 14 days and the 84-day absence is a concern, though Sean Bowen's booking keeps him in the picture from the rear.

runners_data.name: Caspada
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's five-year-old has won once and placed once from six runs on Good ground, but OR=94 is career-high and the [STYLE_FIT=0.92] tag flags a small risk of being shuffled back; returned just 19 days ago and sets the pace in what is otherwise a one-dimensional pace shape.

runners_data.name: Poetry Man
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for trainer/jockey combination George and Jonathon Bewley, with a win and two places from 15 sim-going runs; hg:tv (tongue-tie/visor) may sharpen him, but he has shown PU/pulled-up marks and form figures suggest he fades when challenged, so his ability to sustain a front-running effort is questionable.

runners_data.name: Imperial Rule
runners_data.note: Lizzie Quinlan's nine-year-old is the form pick on recent Good-ground form — a winner 36 days ago and three wins from 14 Good runs; hg:t (tongue-tie) in place, Sean Quinlan up for his wife's yard, and the return to a longer trip suits his strong-travelling hold-up style.

runners_data.name: Kantagua Du Large
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a solid recent record at distances of 24-25f, though sim-going returns show 0W0P from 10 relevant runs — the cleanest form flag of concern in the field; Clive Boultbee-Brooks is 0/3 in 14 days and the horse wears a tongue-strap.

runners_data.name: Ballynoe Boy
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards' six-year-old is a natural hold-up horse whose true style sits at the rear; placed twice from eight Good runs and quick turnaround (15 days) suggests he is fit, but on this tight track he will need a clear run that may not materialise from a packed midfield.

runners_data.name: Masterminding
runners_data.note: James Moffatt's seven-year-old ran second on Good 34 days ago at 22f — the form is live — but his genuine rear-of-field style is compromised by redistribution into midfield; Leah Noreci claims 10lb, which is useful weight relief, though the 10/15 sim-going sample (0W1P) is modest.

runners_data.name: Seeyainthesuninn
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's six-year-old returned a pulled-up effort last time and has placed once from 11 sim-going starts; a five-pound claimer in Joshua Thompson takes the ride, and the horse's true hold-up style will be squeezed in a midfield full of similarly natural rear-runners.

runners_data.name: Roi Du Roume
runners_data.note: Only two days since last run is the standout flag here — Mickey Bowen's six-year-old wears a tongue-strap and has placed four times from eight Good starts, but the near-immediate turnaround after a second demands scrutiny; five-pound claimer Shane Fenelon takes the mount.

runners_data.name: Path Of Stars
runners_data.note: Won on Good over 22f 34 days ago for Seamus Mullins, and 10/15 sim-going runs have produced a win and six places — strong recent evidence on this ground; his true hold-up style is being mapped closer than natural, but his form is the most compelling of the redistributed group.

runners_data.name: Alvesta
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER — James Moffatt's five-year-old has been withdrawn and plays no part; the absence removes one of the more interesting Good-ground performers in the field (1W4P from 15 sim-going runs).

runners_data.name: Wakey Wakey Man
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER — OR=95 would have been the top weight and Cian Collins' six-year-old had solid Good-ground form with a place and multiple near-misses; the withdrawal materially reduces field quality at the head of the market and simplifies the race around Caspada's pace.

races.paceDynamic: Caspada is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no meaningful rival to pressurise her from the outside, she is set to control the gallop from the front at Cartmel over 2m6f on Good ground — a configuration that typically produces a measured, sustainable tempo rather than a true test of stamina. Poetry Man is the only other prominent-style runner, and while he may attempt to share the early lead, he has shown a tendency to fade and is unlikely to sustain a genuine challenge for the lead throughout. The rest of the field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up horses — Fine As Wine, Imperial Rule, Kantagua Du Large and the redistributed group of Ballynoe Boy, Masterminding, Seeyainthesuninn, Roi Du Roume, Path Of Stars and Alvesta — meaning those seeking to race closer than their natural position will create compression in mid-division rather than genuine early pace. This race shape strongly favours a horse who can travel prominently behind the controlled front-running Caspada and produce a sustained gallop from the second-last, or alternatively a genuinely good ground mover who can close efficiently from a midfield berth; hold-up horses racing out of role and squeezed into midfield will struggle to find the clear run they need on this tight course.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Caspada Controls, Closers Charge
scenarios.trigger: If Caspada dictates an unchallenged, even gallop and the field settles into a compact pack, leaving the race to be decided by those who travel best through the race.
scenarios.body: If Caspada dictates an unchallenged, even gallop and the field settles into a compact pack, leaving the race to be decided by those who travel best through the race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Good Ground Movers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the Good ground plays genuinely fast and rewards horses with the best recent form at this trip on similar conditions.
scenarios.body: If the Good ground plays genuinely fast and rewards horses with the best recent form at this trip on similar conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Caspada's controlled lead proves slower than it appears and any attempted prominent horses tire from fighting for position, creating a strong-pace-to-finish dynamic for genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: If Caspada's controlled lead proves slower than it appears and any attempted prominent horses tire from fighting for position, creating a strong-pace-to-finish dynamic for genuine hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If Poetry Man pushes forward to challenge Caspada early and the two engage in a genuine pace duel from the start.
scenarios.body: If Poetry Man pushes forward to challenge Caspada early and the two engage in a genuine pace duel from the start.

watchPoints.text: Caspada carries a [STYLE_FIT=0.92] flag — if she is nudged back from her front-running berth in the early stages, the race loses its only genuine pace-setter and the tempo could become erratic or collapse entirely, distorting every scenario.

Path Of Stars and Imperial Rule are the two most interesting form horses but both have their natural hold-up styles compressed into midfield alongside five other redistributed horses — monitor the early stages for crowding and blocked runs on Cartmel's tight circuit.

Roi Du Roume runs just two days after his last outing; watch the market move and paddock demeanour carefully, as a horse that has raced so recently on Good ground may show fatigue at a crucial stage of the race.

Poetry Man's ability or inability to accompany Caspada in the early stages is the clearest race-shape indicator — if he drops away quickly after the first two hurdles, the race is Caspada's to control uncontested; if he pushes forward, assess whether genuine pace has been injected.

With both non-runners (Alvesta and Wakey Wakey Man) gone, the effective field is 10 — the remaining weight at the top of the handicap is compressed between OR=91 and OR=95 represented by Caspada, meaning the handicapper's assessment of the front end is tighter than it first appears.

races.name: Campbell & Rowley Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Sea The Clouds
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 118 and the clear pace-setter here, but the STYLE_FIT tag flags this as a horse racing slightly out of its most productive role; 10/15 on similar going is modest, and the burden of 168lbs after 32 days off tempers confidence despite a recent Soft-ground win.

runners_data.name: Miss Manzor
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained six-year-old for Sean Bowen, arriving 14 days after her last run with 0W0P from 14 similar-going efforts, which is a meaningful red flag; pure hold-up style at Cartmel's tight turns is a tactical challenge and her form string of 4P/P56 suggests consistency issues.

runners_data.name: It's All About You
runners_data.note: 292 days off the track is a serious concern despite the tongue strap and two wins from 15 Good-ground starts; prominent racer for Jennie Candlish whose best form came over shorter at 16f, and stepping up to 2m6f on return from a long absence asks significant questions.

runners_data.name: Nakassama
runners_data.note: Lightly burdened at OR 111 with a genuine hold-up style that suits a truly-run race; recent win at 22f on Good and a placed run at 16f on Soft give him versatility, and the amateur rider (5lb claim) partially offsets the concern of a tight-track test.

runners_data.name: Dinons
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old but remarkably consistent, with 2W4P from 15 similar-going starts and placed efforts at 24f on Good; hold-up style suits a truly-run race and Brian Ellison has him fit on a 22-day turnaround, though age and OR 110 mean he needs everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Pyramid Place
runners_data.note: Held up by nature and last won when the pace was genuine; form string 058P-6 raises fitness and reliability concerns, and 2W2P from 15 similar-going runs is a moderate record — the 22-day gap with a first-time flag of 13F (likely front-runner marker elsewhere) adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Heart Above
runners_data.note: Won at 21f on Good just 35 days ago for Dianne Sayer and Danny McMenamin, which is arguably the standout piece of recent form in the race; prominent racer who can hold a natural position in this field, and 2W4P from 15 similar-going runs supports his claims in a steady-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Divilabother
runners_data.note: Exceptional 13/15 Good-ground strike rate is the most compelling pace-shape statistic in the field; won at 24f on Good most recently and is a confirmed prominent racer likely to secure his natural position, making him a prime beneficiary of the dominant scenario with Robert Dunne in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Feach Amach
runners_data.note: Won at 21f on Good and holds course-related form, but 87 days since last run is a notable absence and the tongue strap hints at management; 2W3P from 15 similar-going efforts is solid, and Ryan Mania's experience gives confidence he can slot in prominently if needed.

runners_data.name: Rauzan
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose natural position has been displaced by the volume of closers in this field; 0W0P from 15 similar-going runs is a stark record, and while the OR 105 and Lizzie Quinlan yard have placed horses before, the redistribution compounds an already difficult profile.

runners_data.name: Evenwood Sonofagun
runners_data.note: Holds a vital course-and-distance win at 26f on Good which is directly relevant form; prominent racer who is likely to find his position in this field, and Sean Quinlan's big-race experience is an asset — 2W5P from 15 similar-going runs underlines that Good ground genuinely suits.

runners_data.name: Secret Secret
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer for James Moffatt carrying Brian Hughes, but the field's density means the horse is likely to find itself further back than ideal; 0W1P from 15 similar-going starts is a poor record and OR 99 is the lowest among the Moffatt trio, dampening expectations.

runners_data.name: Jack Sprat
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago, which is a significant concern that will affect freshness and jumping sharpness; a true hold-up type squeezed rearward by field depth, and 0W3P from 15 similar-going runs — while placed — suggests a horse that finds ways to finish without winning.

runners_data.name: Butty O Brien
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner so cannot take part; was a natural prominent type whose redistribution to midfield was already flagged, and his absence slightly reduces the congestion problem among the prominent group, leaving more space for Divilabother and Evenwood Sonofagun.

races.paceDynamic: Sea The Clouds is the lone confirmed front runner and, with no rival willing or able to dispute the lead, will dictate a controlled, honest pace across 2m6f on Good ground at Cartmel. The prominent brigade — Heart Above, Divilabother, Feach Amach, Evenwood Sonofagun and It's All About You — will track close behind, creating a compact lead group that keeps the gallop respectable without turning it into a cavalry charge. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Butty O Brien, Secret Secret, Rauzan and Jack Sprat are all flagged as redistributed, meaning their natural positions are genuinely compromised and they are likely to race in unfamiliar spots — Divilabother and Evenwood Sonofagun are best-placed among the prominent types to actually secure the position they want. A genuine, uncontested pace from Sea The Clouds over an extended trip on Good ground at a tight, turning track favours closers and prominent racers who can travel fluidly and deliver a sustained finish — horses with clean jumping, strong Good-ground form and the stamina to grind out the distance are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.title: Steady Lead, Closers Fire
scenarios.trigger: If Sea The Clouds sets an honest but uncontested gallop and the race is run at a true, even tempo that sets it up for those tracking within three lengths.
scenarios.body: If Sea The Clouds sets an honest but uncontested gallop and the race is run at a true, even tempo that sets it up for those tracking within three lengths.

scenarios.label: B

scenarios.body: If Divilabother and Evenwood Sonofagun secure their natural positions just behind Sea The Clouds and kick decisively from two out before the hold-up brigade can respond.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Sea The Clouds sets a stronger-than-expected gallop that stretches the field and opens a route for true closers to deliver a late run down the outside.
scenarios.body: If Sea The Clouds sets a stronger-than-expected gallop that stretches the field and opens a route for true closers to deliver a late run down the outside.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runs On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even slower than expected and Sea The Clouds is allowed to coast, conserving enough energy to maintain a clear lead into the straight unchallenged.
scenarios.body: If the pace is even slower than expected and Sea The Clouds is allowed to coast, conserving enough energy to maintain a clear lead into the straight unchallenged.

watchPoints.text: Divilabother's 13/15 Good-ground record is the standout pace-shape statistic — watch whether Robert Dunne slots him cleanly into the prominent group early, because if he does, that form suggests he will be very hard to pass.

Jack Sprat ran only two days ago — watch for any signs of jumping errors or flagging stamina in the closing stages, as horses returning on such a quick turnaround over 2m6f on Good at Cartmel are vulnerable to errors at the final flights.

Sea The Clouds sets the pace but carries 168lbs and is tagged with a STYLE_FIT concern — watch the early gallop closely; if the pace is too slow it could flatter the front runner, but if rivals push closer than expected it could unravel quickly.

Evenwood Sonofagun holds a course-and-distance win at 26f on Good — watch whether Sean Quinlan gets him into a prominent position early, as the trip and ground are squarely in his favour and a clean round would give him every chance.

Butty O Brien is a declared non-runner — connections and punters should confirm the final field, as his absence changes the prominent-runner dynamics slightly and may ease the positional battle for Divilabother and Feach Amach.

races.name: Oakmere Homes Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Zillow
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from Willie Mullins, stepping down in trip after a string of poor efforts in heavy-ground staying races; his best form (a win at 16f on Soft) came at shorter and on different ground, and Good going here may suit better, though the 85-day absence adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Fiveonefive
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with headgear (p), whose record on Good ground is deeply unimpressive (0W0P from 9 comparable runs); 34 days since last run is fine, but the combination of running style and going record makes him a difficult fit for this race shape.

runners_data.name: High Court Cave
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner by designation, though the STYLE_FIT flag notes he is racing somewhat out of role — his form includes a win and placed efforts on Good ground and he holds tactical advantage as the only horse likely to lead, but that role brings pressure in a tight finish.

runners_data.name: Filibustering
runners_data.note: In-form prominent racer who has won twice recently on Good ground (at 16f and 17f), making him a natural fit for this pace shape; headgear (t) worn, and the 57-day absence with a 32-day flag is mild concern, but Harry Derham's 1/6 T14 suggests the yard is ticking over.

runners_data.name: Miss Maverick
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with excellent Good-ground form (3W3P from 7 similar runs), 15 days since last run keeps her fresh, and the slight drop back from 20f trips to 2m1f may sharpen her finishing effort; Gary Hanmer yet to fire in the 14-day window (0/10) but James Davies takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Amancio
runners_data.note: Genuinely a front-running type by style — well-schooled over hurdles with wins on Soft and Good — but the field's pace congestion means she is unlikely to get her natural position; 197 days off (with a flags marker) is a significant fitness question, and the 5yo is relatively lightly-raced over hurdles.

runners_data.name: Banderas
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two wins on Good and a decent recent record; ran just 40 days ago (13-day flag), headgear (t) worn, and Sam England's yard is in decent nick (T14: 6/15) — profiles as an each-way type if the pace quickens and stragglers are caught.

runners_data.name: Nap Hand
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose Good-ground record (1W7P from 10 runs) shows he fires on this surface without always winning; Tom Cannon is a strong booking, and 55 days since last run (36-day flag) is worth monitoring — best suited to a scenario where the pace quickens and the short Cartmel straight doesn't punish his style.

runners_data.name: Bittalemon
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse tagged as redistributed — placed into the midfield map position because rear slots are oversubscribed — so his true closing style may be compromised; 32 days since last run is fine, apprentice Leah Noreci (10lbs) is a notable claim, and his best win came at 17f on Good.

runners_data.name: Winds Of Winter
runners_data.note: Runs just seven days after his last outing, a very quick turnaround; this is a true prominent racer squeezed into a midfield slot by field congestion, reducing his likely impact, and the Bewley yard has had no T14 winners from three runners — the style compromise and trainer form combine to temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Goodwin Face
runners_data.note: Cracking recent form with two wins and two placed efforts on Good ground at similar trips — genuinely progressive — but as a natural prominent racer displaced to midfield by pace volume, securing his desired position will be a challenge; ran just two days ago (flags: very quick turnaround) which is the single biggest concern about his participation here.

races.paceDynamic: High Court Cave is the lone confirmed front-runner and will lead from the off, setting a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 2m1f on Good ground at Cartmel — a track where a controlled pace from the front is a significant weapon. With no credible rivals willing to challenge for the lead, High Court Cave can dictate terms throughout, rationing his effort and potentially stretching the field on the final turn. The field holds more prominent-leaning types than can all occupy their natural position: Amancio, Goodwin Face, and Winds Of Winter are genuine prominent racers but have been mapped to midfield given the congestion up front, meaning Filibustering and Miss Maverick are the likeliest to actually secure the early prominent berths behind High Court Cave. This race shape — a single uncontested front-runner on a tight, galloping track — strongly favours horses that can race prominently and attack the leader before the final hurdle, making on-pace profiles the clear tactical beneficiaries.

scenarios.title: Controlled lead, prominent strike
scenarios.trigger: If High Court Cave dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominent horses behind him travel fluently.
scenarios.body: If High Court Cave dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominent horses behind him travel fluently.

scenarios.body: If the redistributed prominent types (Goodwin Face, Amancio, Winds Of Winter) force their way forward and create an unexpectedly contested pace.

watchPoints.text: Goodwin Face ran just two days ago — watch market moves and any morning scratchings, as connections may take advantage of a withdrawal declaration; if he lines up, his position in the early stages will be the key tell for whether he can overcome the style displacement.

Miss Maverick's Good-ground record (3W3P) and prominent style make her the most natural beneficiary of this pace shape — watch whether she travels fluently in the slipstream of High Court Cave from flag to flag, as her jumping and position at the second-last will define the race.

Filibustering's 57-day absence (32-day flag) combined with two recent wins means he arrives fit-on-form but potentially race-short; watch his behaviour in the parade ring and how sharply he jumps the early hurdles as indicators of whether the break has sharpened or dulled his edge.

The cluster of Amancio, Winds Of Winter, and Goodwin Face all wanting prominent positions creates a potential crowding flashpoint on Cartmel's tight opening bend — if any of these horses gets shuffled back or loses confidence early, it fundamentally changes the race shape from SCENARIO_A to SCENARIO_D.

High Court Cave carries the STYLE_FIT flag suggesting he may not be fully at ease in the sole front-running role — monitor whether the amateur Mr O McGill (5) sends him forward assertively from the gate or allows him to be taken on, as any hesitation could invite a rival to grab the lead and rewrite the race entirely.

races.name: Oakmere Homes Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Pour Les Filles
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's mare has won on Good ground and is the one confirmed pace-setter, giving her a positional advantage on a track that suits front-runners, though a tongue-tie plus a STYLE_FIT flag at this distance warrants slight caution about whether she can sustain it all the way to 2m5f.

runners_data.name: Light N Strike
runners_data.note: The ten-year-old carries the same OR as Pour Les Filles and has solid Good-ground figures (12 runs, 2W 7P), making him a natural companion just off the pace; his age is a small concern but Shane Fenelon's 5lb claim is a useful weight relief.

runners_data.name: Breizh River
runners_data.note: Consistent recent form (251-32) and a recent Cartmel-style win on Good ground give this horse strong credentials, but it is a natural front-runner that this crowded pace map cannot accommodate cleanly — it may have to work harder than ideal to find its rhythm.

runners_data.name: Buy Some Time
runners_data.note: Four wins on Good going and a recent victory at 2m4f mark this as a lively player on form, yet like Breizh River it is a genuine prominent type forced into a role it may not want; Ryan Mania will need to manufacture the position quickly or it risks racing against its nature.

runners_data.name: Got Grey
runners_data.note: James Moffatt's seven-year-old is the only true hold-up runner in the race and has a sound record at 13 from 15 on Good ground, but Cartmel's tight track militates heavily against late closers and Leah Noreci's 10lb claim means it carries the least weight in the field — both positive and negative factors in play.

runners_data.name: Sean Og
runners_data.note: A recent win (1/21f/GOO) and Dianne Sayer's patient handling suggest this horse arrives fit, but a natural prominent racer carrying the lowest OR (108) in the field is bumped into a midfield slot by the overcrowded pace map and will need Quinlan to find a way forward earlier than the map suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Pour Les Filles is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only six runners at Cartmel's tight, turning track, she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable clip without being seriously harassed for the lead. Breizh River, Buy Some Time, and Sean Og are all natural prominent racers but with Pour Les Filles already occupying that position and the field thin enough that only one or two others can genuinely sit on her girth, at least one of those three will be pushed wider or further back than ideal. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Pour Les Filles and Light N Strike are best placed to actually secure the prominent berths, with Breizh River, Buy Some Time, and Sean Og likely shuffled into roles that do not suit them. A steady-to-fair gallop set by Pour Les Filles over 2m5f on Good ground at a track that rewards jumping fluency and positional racing points clearly to prominent, front-of-the-field runners who can travel sweetly and jump efficiently — hold-up horses have limited room to manoeuvre on this track and will find it hard to close if the pace is not truly punishing.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Breizh River, Buy Some Time, or Sean Og can force their way into prominent positions at the start — if two or three of them manage it, the pace becomes genuinely contested and Pour Les Filles' chance shortens dramatically.

Got Grey's jockey Leah Noreci (10lb claimer) will need to judge the pace perfectly from off it at Cartmel — any misjudgement in positioning on this turning track could leave the hold-up horse with no run.
Light N Strike has a poor overall win-rate (2 from 15 on similar going) despite placing often — monitor in-running to see if it travels sweetly or begins to labour before the home turn.

Cartmel's fences and tight bends place a premium on clean jumping; any horse that makes a significant jumping error at the ditch or the open ditch down the back is unlikely to recover, given the compact nature of this six-runner field with nowhere to hide.

races.name: Holker Hall & Gardens Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Shantou Show
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner who will dictate terms from flag to finish; ten-year-old carrying top weight on good ground he has handled before, though recent form is modest (5-8-5 finishes) and the amateur rider conceding 5lbs adds a further layer of risk at the finish.

runners_data.name: You Did
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has won twice and placed twice in nine similar-going starts, with two recent wins on soft — the step up to good ground here is the key query, but prominent style and Brian Ellison handling a 143-day break make him an interesting runner once fit.

runners_data.name: Halfway House Lad
runners_data.note: Two wins from the last two starts on good ground over this sort of trip are the standout credentials here; the claiming rider Leah Noreci (10) gives 10lbs but the form line is strong and James Moffatt's yard is 0/3 in the last fortnight — worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Judicial Review
runners_data.note: Had his last run only two days ago which is unusual and worth flagging as a potential concern; prominent style suits the likely race shape, but a P-9-P recent form sequence and headgear combination (tongue-tie, blinkers) suggest a horse that can be inconsistent — Brian Hughes is a strong booking.

runners_data.name: Lights Are Green
runners_data.note: Strong good-ground handler (11/15 runs on similar surface) whose natural racing style is prominent, though the congested pace map means he is unlikely to get his preferred tracking position and may find himself racing with less cover than ideal — Jonathon Bewley is an able pilot if gaps appear.

runners_data.name: Blazing Court
runners_data.note: Front-running by nature but pushed into a midfield role on this map given the volume of prominent types; carries a P-U-U-5-4 recent sequence including two unseated-rider incidents and has not won since moving up in distance — the amateur partner and sketchy jumping record compound the risk.

runners_data.name: Star Turn
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose two most recent completions have produced second-place finishes on good ground over a similar trip; Sean Bowen is a significant jockey booking and Mickey Bowen's yard is in excellent form (4/23 in 14 days) — needs a stronger pace than Shantou Show is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Croagh Patrick

runners_data.name: Aill Dubh
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has recorded a win and a third on soft ground recently but has no similar-going wins or places in 14 runs — the good ground here is a real concern that the race shape cannot overcome alone for a horse who depends on late pace to be produced.

runners_data.name: Kingofthegame
runners_data.note: Won his last start over today's trip on good ground at Cartmel, giving him outstanding course-and-distance form credentials; naturally prominent but the crowded pace map relegates him to a midfield role in this analysis — Ryan Mania may seek to push forward early to reclaim his natural position.

races.paceDynamic: Shantou Show is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to press for the lead from the off, will control the tempo throughout this 3m1½f trip at Cartmel on good ground. The pace is expected to be honest but sustainable — Shantou Show's rider Mr D McGill will almost certainly dictate from the front without serious harassment, creating a steady, rhythm-based gallop that rewards those who travel well within themselves. Lights Are Green, Blazing Court, and Kingofthegame are all natural prominent racers but the field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — of the three, Lights Are Green (course form, good-ground handler) and Halfway House Lad (in-form, suited by trip) are best positioned to secure the closer tracking slots, while Blazing Court and Kingofthegame are likely to find themselves racing further back than ideal. With a controlled, single-paced gallop virtually guaranteed, this race shape strongly favours genuine staying prominents who can slot in close to the leader and produce a sustained jump-for-jump effort in the straight — hold-up horses will need a late injection of pace that may simply not materialise.

Judicial Review ran just two days ago and connections have not declared any reason publicly — monitor market moves and paddock demeanour, as a horse that has raced so recently in a handicap chase over 3m1½f on good ground is unusual and could flag a stable or fitness concern.

Blazing Court has unseated his rider in two of his last four starts and is a natural front-runner who will be racing out of position — watch for jumping errors or erratic behaviour in the early stages that could unsettle the field behind him.

Star Turn is trained by Mickey Bowen, whose yard has hit a 4/23 strike rate in the last 14 days, and is ridden by son Sean Bowen — if the pace quickens appreciably in the final mile, this combination has the credentials to finish faster than the race shape currently suggests.

runners_data.name: Dexter

runners_data.name: Clean Getaway

runners_data.name: Zumbi
runners_data.note: Non-runner — disregard for this race.

races.paceDynamic: Bentley Road is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to challenge her for the lead, Derek Fox should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over Cartmel's tight 2m1½f circuit. Conquer The Breeze, Dream Jet, and Blue Reed are the prominent types most likely to track closely behind, creating a compact front group but without the friction to force Bentley Road into burning energy early. The field contains more hold-up horses than can realistically operate deep — Cuzco Du Mathan, Dexter, and Clean Getaway are all genuine closers redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning the rear of the field is less loaded with true stalkers than it appears, and the complexion is front-end dominated. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-lead profiles: with a single pace-setter setting a comfortable tempo on a sharp, turning track, horses who can travel close to the fractions without expending energy will be ideally placed when the race quickens after the last.

watchPoints.text: Conquer The Breeze is arriving just 7 days after her last run — watch her in the pre-parade for any signs of dullness or stiffness that might blunt her usually bold jumping and prominent jumping style.

Blue Reed won her last start over a longer trip and could be forward enough to pressure Bentley Road's lead — if she moves upsides at any stage, the controlled tempo assumption breaks down and the race becomes more truly run, opening the door for hold-up horses.

Cuzco Du Mathan, Dexter, and Clean Getaway are all natural closers compressed into midfield; watch the early stages — if any three of them try to push forward to find a more natural position, there could be crowding and interference on Cartmel's narrow, turning track.

Ghasham's booking of Sean Bowen is the standout jockey upgrade in the race — if the pace is genuinely decent through the middle stages, Bowen's ability to time a late challenge from the hold-up position makes her the most dangerous outside of the obvious front-end contenders.

Bentley Road's jumping record over this shorter trip and on good ground is untested at full distance — watch her at the early fences to confirm she travels fluently; any jumping errors under Derek Fox could allow Conquer The Breeze or Dream Jet to steal a significant advantage.
